questions.q: Which real test fails in this lesson's scenario?
options: A test that doesn't exist yet in this project
The `relationships` test on `customer_id`
The `unique` test on `fct_orders.order_id`, added back in Lesson 8
The `accepted_values` test on `status`
questions.explain: The nightly build reports unique_fct_orders_order_id failing with 14 duplicate results.

questions.q: What's the first job after seeing a test failure report?
options: Immediately rewrite the join that's suspected of causing it
Reproduce the problem reliably on your own screen, not fix anything yet
Delete the duplicate rows by hand from fct_orders
Disable the failing test so the build goes green
questions.explain: The first diagnostic step is always reproducing the symptom reliably, before touching any model.

questions.q: What query reproduces the duplicate order_id rows directly?
options: `select order_id, count(*) from fct_orders group by 1 having count(*) > 1`
`select sum(amount) from fct_orders`
`select * from fct_orders where order_id is null`
`select distinct status from fct_orders`
questions.explain: Grouping by order_id and filtering for count greater than 1 surfaces exactly the rows the unique test is flagging.

questions.q: What key fact from isolating the variable points the investigation forward?
options: The test has always failed since the model was first built
The model's SQL was edited yesterday
Power BI's cache is out of date
The test passed cleanly back in Lesson 8, so something changed between then and now — most likely new rows from incremental runs, not the model's SQL
questions.explain: A test that passed earlier and fails now, with no code change, points at data that arrived in between — not a logic bug present from day one.

questions.q: What lead does this lesson point toward, without confirming it yet?
options: A missing index on the customers mart
A typo in the status column's accepted_values list
The payments join flagged back in Lesson 6 as worth watching, since a join that isn't one-row-per-order can duplicate order rows
A Power BI refresh schedule misconfiguration
questions.explain: Lesson 6 explicitly flagged the payments join as something to watch — this lesson's symptom is the first real evidence pointing back at it.
